newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Rentokil leans on BET for growth.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Rentokil leans on BET for growth.

text.p: International business services group Rentokil Initial Plc announced sharp rises in 1996 sales and profits Wednesday, but industry analysts expressed concerns that the group relied heavily on newly acquired BET for progress.

Rentokil Initial, formed last year through Rentokil's hostile takeover of rival BET, said pre-tax profit jumped 48 percent to 318 million pounds ($505.8 million) while sales were up 168 percent at 2.34 billion pounds ($3.73 billion).

The results were at the bottom end of analysts' forecasts of between 317 million ($505 million) and 335 million pounds ($533 million), and the company's stock fell sharply in morning trading, down 5.7 percent.
Rentokil Initial, whose services include office cleaning, personnel, security, pest control and supplying plants, also announced a two-for-one share split.
It said the integration of BET, bought for 2.1 billion pounds ($3.34 billion), "had proceeded rapidly and successfully in line with plans."

However, excluding BET, sales were up 15 percent and profits rose 9 percent to 233.4 million pounds ($371.7 million), raising concerns that the company would not have lived up to its long-established reputation for delivering year-on-year earnings and sales growth of 20 percent without BET.
"People will be asking about their core businesses and wondering whether they would have made the grade without BET," one trader said.
The company said the results had been affected by 16.4 million pounds ($26 million) in integration costs, focusing of management effort on BET's integration and adverse exchange rates.
Chief Executive Sir Clive Thompson said he did not expect the company to make any more large acquisitions for the next two years while it integrated the 52 BET operations.
